edbDesc: A process similar to liquefaction whereby a granular material is converted from a static solid-like state to a dynamic fluid-like state. This process occurs when a fluid (liquid or gas) is passed up through the granular material. When fluidized, a bed of solid particles will behave as a fluid, like a liquid or gas.
title: Fluidization
description: Blow air up through a bed of sand or powder and at a certain speed the grains lift apart and the whole bed starts behaving like a boiling liquid: you can stir it, pour it, and things float or sink in it. Fritz Winkler used it in Germany in 1922 to turn powdered coal into gas. Fluidized beds now crack crude oil into gasoline and burn coal and waste cleanly.
effect: gas blown up through a granular bed makes it flow like a liquid
usedIn: Fluid catalytic cracking in oil refineries (1942)
Fluidized-bed dryers for food and medicines
strength: A gentle updraft of a few centimetres per second is enough; a ball heavier than the sand sinks and a lighter one bobs up.
pickWhy: Specific effect with big industrial uses; not in the deck.
